correctness.rationale: For N iid \(\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)\) velocities, the cycle time is \(L/\max V_i\), with survival \((1-e^{-\lambda L/t})^N\) and finite mean iff \(N\ge2\). Normalized excursion occupation tilts the joint velocity law by reciprocal maximum and produces an independent uniform phase, so the leftmost position is exactly uniform. The scaled exponential maximum \(Y_N/\log N\) tends to 1 and reciprocal concentration plus a finite inverse second moment prove the stationary speed tilt vanishes in total variation. A law-of-large-numbers and bounded-Lipschitz argument yields both joint-tagged and random empirical exponential-mixture limits; the exceedance CDF follows from a monotone uniform transform. The independently run standard-library checker passed exact quadrature, direct cycle survival, finite-N stationary weighting and asymptotic first/second-moment diagnostics. No simulation was used to justify an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The result gives a quantitative coexistence of a uniform macroscopic particle front and a logarithmically compressed random exponential bulk, with a nonvanishing empirical exceedance variance. These new spatial population observables answer a natural many-particle extension beyond earlier single-particle stationary laws and known ballistic search-time formulas, not merely evaluating a pre-existing mean search time. The already known finite-mean \(N\ge2\) cutoff is a premise, not part of its novelty.
